rows.question: Please generate a summary of the closing balances at the end of each month for each customer transactions, show the monthly changes and monthly cumulative bank account balances. Ensure that even if a customer has no account activity in a given month, the balance for that month is still included in the output.

WITH customer_transaction_daily_effects AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
    CASE
      WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
      WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'withdrawal' THEN -txn_amount
      ELSE -txn_amount
    END AS signed_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
),
bounds AS (
  SELECT
    date(min(txn_date), 'start of month') AS min_month_start,
    date(max(txn_date), 'start of month') AS max_month_start
  FROM customer_transactions
),
months AS (
  -- generate month starts between min and max (supports up to 120 months; expand if needed)
  SELECT date(min_month_start, '+' || n || ' months') AS month_start
  FROM bounds, (
    SELECT 0 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5
    UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11
    UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17
    UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19 UNION ALL SELECT 20 UNION ALL SELECT 21 UNION ALL SELECT 22 UNION ALL SELECT 23
    UNION ALL SELECT 24 UNION ALL SELECT 25 UNION ALL SELECT 26 UNION ALL SELECT 27 UNION ALL SELECT 28 UNION ALL SELECT 29
    UNION ALL SELECT 30 UNION ALL SELECT 31 UNION ALL SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34 UNION ALL SELECT 35
    UNION ALL SELECT 36 UNION ALL SELECT 37 UNION ALL SELECT 38 UNION ALL SELECT 39 UNION ALL SELECT 40 UNION ALL SELECT 41
    UNION ALL SELECT 42 UNION ALL SELECT 43 UNION ALL SELECT 44 UNION ALL SELECT 45 UNION ALL SELECT 46 UNION ALL SELECT 47
    UNION ALL SELECT 48 UNION ALL SELECT 49 UNION ALL SELECT 50 UNION ALL SELECT 51 UNION ALL SELECT 52 UNION ALL SELECT 53
    UNION ALL SELECT 54 UNION ALL SELECT 55 UNION ALL SELECT 56 UNION ALL SELECT 57 UNION ALL SELECT 58 UNION ALL SELECT 59
  ) nums
  WHERE date(min_month_start, '+' || n || ' months') <= (SELECT max_month_start FROM bounds)
),
calendar AS (
  SELECT
    date(month_start, 'start of month') AS month_start,
    date(month_start, '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', month_start) AS INTEGER) AS year,
    CAST(strftime('%m', month_start) AS INTEGER) AS month
  FROM months
),
customers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transaction_daily_effects
),
customer_months AS (
  SELECT c.customer_id, cal.month_start, cal.month_end, cal.year, cal.month
  FROM customers c CROSS JOIN calendar cal
),
monthly_net AS (
  -- net amount for each customer in each calendar month (could be zero)
  SELECT
    cm.customer_id,
    cm.year,
    cm.month,
    cm.month_end,
    COALESCE(SUM(d.signed_amount), 0) AS monthly_net_amount,
    CASE WHEN COUNT(d.txn_date) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_activity
  FROM customer_months cm
  LEFT JOIN customer_transaction_daily_effects d
    ON d.customer_id = cm.customer_id
    AND strftime('%Y', d.txn_date) = printf('%04d', cm.year)
    AND strftime('%m', d.txn_date) = printf('%02d', cm.month)
  GROUP BY cm.customer_id, cm.year, cm.month, cm.month_end
),
running AS (
  -- compute cumulative closing balance per month per customer using a window over month order
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    year,
    month,
    month_end,
    monthly_net_amount,
    has_activity,
    SUM(monthly_net_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY year, month ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS closing_balance
  FROM monthly_net
)
SELECT
  customer_id,
  year,
  month,
  month_end AS month_end_date,
  ROUND(closing_balance, 2) AS closing_balance,
  ROUND(closing_balance - LAG(closing_balance) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY year, month), 2) AS monthly_change,
  ROUND(closing_balance, 2) AS cumulative_balance,
  has_activity
FROM running
ORDER BY customer_id, year, month

rows.question: For each customer and each month of 2020, first calculate the month-end balance by adding all deposit amounts and subtracting all withdrawal amounts that occurred during that specific month. Then determine which month in 2020 has the highest count of customers with a positive month-end balance and which month has the lowest count. For each of these two months, compute the average month-end balance across all customers and provide the difference between these two averages

WITH
-- normalize transactions: signed amounts (+ deposit, - otherwise) and yyyy-mm
tx AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
    substr(date(txn_date),1,7) AS txn_yyyy_mm,
    CASE WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END AS signed_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
),
distinct_customers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions
),
-- generate the 12 months of 2020 as strings
months_2020 AS (
  SELECT '2020-01' AS month_yyyy_mm UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-02' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-03' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-04' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-05' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-06' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-07' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-08' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-09' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-10' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-11' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-12'
),
-- per customer per month compute month-end balance (sum of signed amounts in that month)
customer_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    m.month_yyyy_mm,
    COALESCE(SUM(t.signed_amount), 0) AS month_end_balance
  FROM months_2020 m
  CROSS JOIN distinct_customers c
  LEFT JOIN tx t
    ON t.customer_id = c.customer_id
    AND t.txn_yyyy_mm = m.month_yyyy_mm
  GROUP BY c.customer_id, m.month_yyyy_mm
),
-- per month aggregates: count of customers with positive balance and average balance across all customers
month_stats AS (
  SELECT
    month_yyyy_mm,
    SUM(CASE WHEN month_end_balance > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS positive_count,
    AVG(month_end_balance) AS avg_balance
  FROM customer_monthly
  GROUP BY month_yyyy_mm
),
max_month AS (
  SELECT month_yyyy_mm, positive_count, avg_balance
  FROM month_stats
  ORDER BY positive_count DESC, month_yyyy_mm ASC
  LIMIT 1
),
min_month AS (
  SELECT month_yyyy_mm, positive_count, avg_balance
  FROM month_stats
  ORDER BY positive_count ASC, month_yyyy_mm ASC
  LIMIT 1
)
SELECT
  max_month.month_yyyy_mm AS max_month,
  max_month.positive_count AS max_month_positive_customers_count,
  max_month.avg_balance AS max_month_average_month_end_balance,
  min_month.month_yyyy_mm AS min_month,
  min_month.positive_count AS min_month_positive_customers_count,
  min_month.avg_balance AS min_month_average_month_end_balance,
  (max_month.avg_balance - min_month.avg_balance) AS difference_between_averages
FROM max_month, min_month

rows.question: For each customer, group all deposits and withdrawals by the first day of each month to obtain a monthly net amount, then calculate each month’s closing balance by cumulatively summing these monthly nets. Next, determine the most recent month’s growth rate by comparing its closing balance to the prior month’s balance, treating deposits as positive and withdrawals as negative, and if the previous month’s balance is zero, the growth rate should be the current month’s balance multiplied by 100. Finally, compute the percentage of customers whose most recent month shows a growth rate of more than 5%.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_monthly_net_txn AS (
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  -- month_start represented as the month's first day in YYYY-MM-01 format derived from txn_date
  substr(ct.txn_date,1,7) || '-01' AS month_start,
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN lower(ct.txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount
      WHEN lower(ct.txn_type) = 'withdrawal' THEN -ct.txn_amount
      ELSE 0
    END
  ) AS monthly_net
FROM customer_transactions ct
WHERE ct.txn_type IN ('deposit','withdrawal')
GROUP BY ct.customer_id, substr(ct.txn_date,1,7)
),
customer_monthly_closing_balance AS (
SELECT
  cmn.customer_id AS customer_id,
  cmn.month_start AS month_start,
  cmn.monthly_net AS monthly_net,
  (
    SELECT SUM(c2.monthly_net)
    FROM customer_monthly_net_txn c2
    WHERE c2.customer_id = cmn.customer_id
      AND (strftime('%Y-%m-%d', c2.month_start) <= strftime('%Y-%m-%d', cmn.month_start))
  ) AS closing_balance
FROM customer_monthly_net_txn cmn
),
customer_most_recent_month_growth AS (
SELECT
  cmmcb.customer_id AS customer_id,
  cmmcb.month_start AS recent_month_start,
  cmmcb.closing_balance AS recent_closing_balance,
  COALESCE(prev.closing_balance, 0) AS previous_closing_balance,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(prev.closing_balance, 0) = 0 THEN COALESCE(cmmcb.closing_balance, 0) * 100.0
    ELSE (COALESCE(cmmcb.closing_balance, 0) - prev.closing_balance) / prev.closing_balance
  END AS growth_rate
FROM
  -- most recent month per customer from monthly closing balances
  (
    SELECT customer_id, month_start, closing_balance
    FROM customer_monthly_closing_balance c
    WHERE month_start = (
      SELECT MAX(month_start) FROM customer_monthly_closing_balance c2 WHERE c2.customer_id = c.customer_id
    )
  ) AS cmmcb
LEFT JOIN
  -- previous month closing balance (month immediately before recent_month_start)
  customer_monthly_closing_balance prev
ON prev.customer_id = cmmcb.customer_id
AND prev.month_start = (
  SELECT month_start
  FROM customer_monthly_closing_balance p2
  WHERE p2.customer_id = cmmcb.customer_id
    AND p2.month_start < cmmcb.month_start
  ORDER BY p2.month_start DESC
  LIMIT 1
)
)
SELECT
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_most_recent_month_growth WHERE growth_rate > 0.05) AS numerator_customers_with_growth_gt_5,
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM customer_transactions) AS total_customers,
  CASE
    WHEN (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM customer_transactions) = 0 THEN 0.0
    ELSE ( (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_most_recent_month_growth WHERE growth_rate > 0.05) * 1.0
           / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM customer_transactions) ) * 100.0
  END AS percentage_customers_with_growth_gt_5

rows.question: For each month, calculate the total balance from all users for the previous month (measured as of the 1st of each month), replacing any negative balances with zero. Ensure that data from the first month is used only as a baseline for calculating previous total balance, and exclude it from the final output. Sort the results in ascending order by month.

WITH customer_running_balance_at_month_start AS (
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  DATE(substr(ct.txn_date,1,4) || '-' || substr(ct.txn_date,6,2) || '-01') AS month_start_date,
  (
    SELECT IFNULL(SUM(txn_amount),0)
    FROM customer_transactions t2
    WHERE t2.customer_id = ct.customer_id
      AND DATE(t2.txn_date) < DATE(substr(ct.txn_date,1,4) || '-' || substr(ct.txn_date,6,2) || '-01')
  ) AS raw_balance
FROM customer_transactions ct
GROUP BY ct.customer_id, month_start_date
),
customer_months AS (
SELECT
  substr(txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01' AS month_start_date,
  MIN(txn_date) AS example_txn_date
FROM customer_transactions
WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL AND trim(txn_date) <> ''
GROUP BY substr(txn_date, 1, 7)
),
customer_transaction_rows AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  -- normalize txn_date to ISO YYYY-MM-DD where possible: assume input is already YYYY-MM-DD or similar; try substrings for common formats
  CASE
    WHEN length(txn_date) = 10 AND txn_date LIKE '%-%' THEN
      -- assume already YYYY-MM-DD or DD-MM-YYYY; disambiguate: if first four chars are year numeric -> keep
      CASE WHEN substr(txn_date,1,4) GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]' THEN txn_date
           -- if format is DD-MM-YYYY convert to YYYY-MM-DD
           WHEN substr(txn_date,3,1) = '-' AND substr(txn_date,6,1) = '-' THEN
             substr(txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(txn_date,1,2)
           ELSE txn_date END
    WHEN txn_date LIKE '%/%' THEN
      -- handle formats like DD/MM/YY or DD/MM/YYYY or D/M/YY etc.
      -- try to parse as DD/MM/YYYY -> convert
      CASE
        WHEN length(txn_date) >= 8 AND substr(txn_date, instr(txn_date,'/')+1,1) GLOB '[0-9]' THEN
          -- split by '/' using simple substring functions: assume DD/MM/YYYY
          (CASE
             WHEN length(txn_date) = 10 THEN substr(txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(txn_date,1,2)
             WHEN length(txn_date) = 8 THEN
               -- assume D/M/YY -> convert to 20YY with zero-pad
               '20' || substr(txn_date,7,2) || '-' || printf('%02d', CAST(substr(txn_date,4,1) AS INTEGER)) || '-' || printf('%02d', CAST(substr(txn_date,1,1) AS INTEGER))
             ELSE txn_date END)
        ELSE txn_date
      END
    ELSE txn_date
  END AS txn_date,
  txn_amount,
  txn_type
FROM customer_transactions
)
SELECT
  cm.month_start_date,
  SUM(CASE WHEN cr.raw_balance < 0 THEN 0 ELSE cr.raw_balance END) AS total_balance
FROM customer_months cm
JOIN customer_running_balance_at_month_start cr
  ON cr.month_start_date = cm.month_start_date
WHERE cm.month_start_date > (SELECT MIN(month_start_date) FROM customer_months)
GROUP BY cm.month_start_date
HAVING total_balance IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY cm.month_start_date ASC

rows.question: For a bank database with customer transactions, calculate each customer's daily running balance (where deposits add to the balance and other transaction types subtract). For each customer and each day, compute the 30-day rolling average balance (only after having 30 days of data, and treating negative averages as zero). Then group these daily averages by month and find each customer's maximum 30-day average balance within each month. Sum these maximum values across all customers for each month. Consider the first month of each customer's transaction history as the baseline period and exclude it from the final results, presenting monthly totals of these summed maximum 30-day average balances.

WITH customer_transaction_daily_effects AS (
SELECT
  customer_transactions.customer_id AS customer_id,
  date(substr(customer_transactions.txn_date,1,10)) AS txn_date,
  CASE
    WHEN lower(customer_transactions.txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN customer_transactions.txn_amount
    WHEN lower(customer_transactions.txn_type) = 'withdrawal' THEN -customer_transactions.txn_amount
    ELSE -customer_transactions.txn_amount
  END AS signed_amount,
  CASE WHEN customer_transactions.txn_amount IS NOT NULL AND customer_transactions.txn_amount != 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_activity
FROM customer_transactions
),
customer_daily_end_balance AS (
SELECT
  d.customer_id,
  d.txn_date AS calendar_date,
  (
    -- running sum of signed amounts up to and including this date
    SELECT IFNULL(SUM(ctde.signed_amount), 0)
    FROM customer_transaction_daily_effects ctde
    WHERE ctde.customer_id = d.customer_id
      AND DATE(ctde.txn_date) <= DATE(d.txn_date)
  ) AS end_of_day_balance
FROM
  customer_transaction_daily_effects d
),
customer_30day_avg_balance AS (
SELECT
  d.customer_id,
  d.calendar_date AS calendar_date,
  AVG(d2.end_of_day_balance) AS avg_30day_balance,

FROM customer_daily_end_balance d
JOIN customer_daily_end_balance d2
  ON d.customer_id = d2.customer_id
  AND date(d2.calendar_date) BETWEEN date(d.calendar_date, '-29 days') AND date(d.calendar_date)
GROUP BY d.customer_id, d.calendar_date
HAVING COUNT(d2.end_of_day_balance) = 30
),
customer_monthly_max_30day_avg AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  substr(calendar_date,1,7) AS month,
  MAX(avg_30day_balance) AS max_30day_avg
FROM
  customer_30day_avg_balance
GROUP BY
  customer_id,
  substr(calendar_date,1,7)
)
SELECT
  m.month,
  SUM(COALESCE(
        CASE WHEN m.max_30day_avg > 0 THEN m.max_30day_avg ELSE 0 END
      , 0)) AS sum_max_30day_avg_balance
FROM
  (SELECT DISTINCT month FROM customer_monthly_max_30day_avg) months
  CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions) c -- ensure every customer considered per month
  LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_max_30day_avg m
    ON m.month = months.month

    SELECT customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', min(txn_date)) AS first_month
    FROM customer_transactions
    GROUP BY customer_id
  ) fm

WHERE
  -- exclude each customer's first transaction month
  (fm.first_month IS NULL OR m.month IS NULL OR m.month <> fm.first_month)
GROUP BY
  m.month
ORDER BY
  m.month ASC

rows.question: For each customer, calculate their daily balances for every day between their earliest and latest transaction dates, including days without transactions by carrying forward the previous day's balance. Treat any negative daily balances as zero. Then, for each month, determine the highest daily balance each customer had during that month. Finally, for each month, sum these maximum daily balances across all customers to obtain a monthly total.

WITH customer_daily_transactions AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
    lower(txn_type) AS txn_type,
    txn_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
),
customer_date_ranges AS (
  SELECT customer_id, MIN(txn_date) AS min_date, MAX(txn_date) AS max_date
  FROM customer_daily_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
-- numbers 0..999 (adjust if customer spans >1000 days)
nums AS (
  SELECT 0 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4
  UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9
),
numbers AS (
  SELECT (a.n + 10*b.n + 100*c.n) AS n
  FROM nums a, nums b, nums c
),
customer_calendar AS (
  SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    date(c.min_date, '+' || n.n || ' days') AS calendar_date
  FROM customer_date_ranges c
  JOIN numbers n
    ON date(c.min_date, '+' || n.n || ' days') <= c.max_date
),
customer_daily_net AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_date,
    SUM(
      CASE txn_type
        WHEN 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
        WHEN 'withdrawal' THEN -txn_amount
        ELSE txn_amount
      END
    ) AS net_amount
  FROM customer_daily_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id, txn_date
),
-- for each calendar date join net_amount (if any) then compute running sum per customer by date using window
customer_calendar_with_net AS (
  SELECT
    cc.customer_id,
    cc.calendar_date,
    IFNULL(n.net_amount, 0) AS net_amount
  FROM customer_calendar cc
  LEFT JOIN customer_daily_net n
    ON n.customer_id = cc.customer_id
   AND n.txn_date = cc.calendar_date

customer_daily_cumulative AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    calendar_date,
    -- running sum ordered by calendar_date per customer
    SUM(net_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY calendar_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_balance
  FROM customer_calendar_with_net
),
customer_daily_nonneg AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    calendar_date,
    CASE WHEN cumulative_balance < 0 THEN 0 ELSE cumulative_balance END AS daily_balance
  FROM customer_daily_cumulative
),
customer_monthly_max_daily_balance AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    strftime('%Y-%m', calendar_date) AS month,
    MAX(daily_balance) AS max_daily_balance
  FROM customer_daily_nonneg
  GROUP BY customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', calendar_date)
)
SELECT
  month,
  SUM(max_daily_balance) AS monthly_total_max_balances
FROM customer_monthly_max_daily_balance

rows.question: Can you provide a breakdown of how many times each product was viewed, how many times they were added to the shopping cart, and how many times they were left in the cart without being purchased? Also, give me the count of actual purchases for each product. Ensure that products with a page id in (1, 2, 12, 13) are filtered out.

WITH shopping_cart_events_mapped AS (
SELECT
  e.visit_id,
  e.cookie_id,
  e.page_id,
  p.product_id,
  p.page_name,
  e.event_type,
  i.event_name,
  e.sequence_number,
  e.event_time
FROM shopping_cart_events e
JOIN shopping_cart_page_hierarchy p
  ON e.page_id = p.page_id
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_event_identifier i
  ON e.event_type = i.event_type
WHERE e.page_id IS NOT NULL
  AND p.product_id IS NOT NULL
),
product_page_catalog AS (
SELECT
  CAST(shopping_cart_page_hierarchy.product_id AS TEXT) AS product_id,
  shopping_cart_page_hierarchy.page_id AS page_id,
  shopping_cart_page_hierarchy.page_name AS product_name
FROM shopping_cart_page_hierarchy
WHERE shopping_cart_page_hierarchy.product_id IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  e.product_id,
  pc.product_name AS product_name,
  SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name = 'Page View' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS views_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name = 'Add to Cart' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS add_to_cart_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name = 'Purchase' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS purchases_count,
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN e.event_name = 'Add to Cart' AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM shopping_cart_events_mapped p
        WHERE p.product_id = e.product_id
          AND p.event_name = 'Purchase'
          AND (
            (e.visit_id IS NOT NULL AND p.visit_id = e.visit_id)
            OR (e.visit_id IS NULL AND p.cookie_id = e.cookie_id)
          )
          AND p.event_time > e.event_time
          AND p.page_id NOT IN (1,2,12,13)
      ) THEN 1
      ELSE 0
    END
  ) AS abandoned_count
FROM shopping_cart_events_mapped e
LEFT JOIN product_page_catalog pc
  ON e.product_id = pc.product_id
WHERE e.page_id NOT IN (1,2,12,13)
  AND e.event_name IN ('Page View','Add to Cart','Purchase')
GROUP BY e.product_id, pc.product_name
ORDER BY purchases_count DESC, e.product_id ASC

    match_id,
    innings_no,
    over_id,
    SUM(COALESCE(extra_runs,0)) AS extra_runs
  FROM extra_runs
  GROUP BY match_id, innings_no, over_id
),
over_bowler_lookup AS (
  SELECT
    match_id,
    innings_no,
    over_id,
    MIN(bowler) AS bowler
  FROM ball_by_ball
  GROUP BY match_id, innings_no, over_id
),
-- all overs with totals and bowler
overs_with_totals AS (
  SELECT
    obl.match_id,
    obl.innings_no,
    obl.over_id,
    obl.bowler,
    COALESCE(obr.batsman_runs,0) + COALESCE(oer.extra_runs,0) AS over_total_runs
  FROM over_bowler_lookup obl
  LEFT JOIN over_batsman_runs_agg obr USING(match_id, innings_no, over_id)
  LEFT JOIN over_extra_runs_agg oer USING(match_id, innings_no, over_id)
),
-- pick the single over with highest total per match & innings
highest_over_per_innings AS (
  SELECT
    o1.match_id,
    o1.innings_no,
    o1.over_id,
    o1.bowler,
    o1.over_total_runs
  FROM overs_with_totals o1
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM overs_with_totals o2
    WHERE o2.match_id = o1.match_id
      AND o2.innings_no = o1.innings_no
      AND (o2.over_total_runs > o1.over_total_runs
           OR (o2.over_total_runs = o1.over_total_runs AND o2.over_id < o1.over_id))
  )
)
SELECT
  hopi.match_id,
  hopi.innings_no,
  hopi.over_id,
  hopi.bowler,
  hopi.over_total_runs,
  (SELECT AVG(over_total_runs) FROM highest_over_per_innings) AS average_highest_over_runs
FROM highest_over_per_innings hopi

rows.question: For each IPL season, identify the top three batsmen with the highest total runs scored and the top three bowlers with the most wickets taken, excluding ‘run out’, ‘hit wicket’, and ‘retired hurt’ dismissals. In the event of ties in runs or wickets, break the tie using the smaller player ID. Then output these six players in matched positions—batsman 1 with bowler 1, batsman 2 with bowler 2, and batsman 3 with bowler 3—in ascending order of the season ID, along with each player’s total runs or wickets.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH ball_striker_link AS (
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.striker
FROM
  ball_by_ball b
),
bowler_wickets_per_match_player AS (
SELECT
  wt.match_id AS match_id,
  b.bowler AS bowler_id,
  COUNT(*) AS wickets_in_match
FROM wicket_taken wt
JOIN ball_by_ball b
  ON wt.match_id = b.match_id
  AND wt.over_id = b.over_id
  AND wt.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND wt.innings_no = b.innings_no
WHERE wt.kind_out NOT IN ('run out', 'hit wicket', 'retired hurt')
GROUP BY wt.match_id, b.bowler
),
match_season AS (
SELECT
  m.match_id,
  m.season_id,
  m.match_date,
  m.team_1,
  m.team_2
FROM match AS m
),
batsman_runs_per_match_player AS (
SELECT
  bs.match_id,
  bb.striker AS player_id,
  SUM(bs.runs_scored) AS runs_in_match
FROM
  batsman_scored bs
JOIN
  ball_striker_link bb
  ON bs.match_id = bb.match_id
  AND bs.over_id = bb.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = bb.ball_id
  AND bs.innings_no = bb.innings_no
GROUP BY
  bs.match_id,
  bb.striker
)
SELECT
  b.season_id,
  b.batsman_rank AS batsman_rank,
  b.batsman_id,
  b.batsman_total_runs,
  bw.bowler_rank AS bowler_rank,
  bw.bowler_id,
  bw.bowler_total_wickets
FROM
  (
    SELECT
      season_id,
      player_id AS batsman_id,
      SUM(runs_in_match) AS batsman_total_runs,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY season_id ORDER BY SUM(runs_in_match) DESC, player_id ASC) AS batsman_rank
    FROM batsman_runs_per_match_player br
    JOIN match_season ms USING (match_id)
    GROUP BY season_id, player_id
  ) b
LEFT JOIN
  (
    SELECT
      season_id,
      bowler_id,
      SUM(wickets_in_match) AS bowler_total_wickets,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY season_id ORDER BY SUM(wickets_in_match) DESC, bowler_id ASC) AS bowler_rank
    FROM bowler_wickets_per_match_player bwmp
    JOIN match_season ms USING (match_id)
    GROUP BY season_id, bowler_id
  ) bw
ON b.season_id = bw.season_id AND b.batsman_rank = bw.bowler_rank
WHERE b.batsman_rank <= 3
ORDER BY b.season_id ASC, b.batsman_rank ASC

rows.question: Find the IDs of players who scored the highest number of partnership runs for each match. The output should include the IDs of two players, each with their individual scores and the total partnership score. For each pair, the player with the higher individual score should be listed as player 1, and the player with the lower score as player 2. In cases where both players have the same score, the player with the higher ID should be player 1, and the player with the lower ID should be player 2. There can be multiple rows for a single match.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH ball_striker_link AS (
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.striker
FROM
  ball_by_ball b
),
ball_bat_pair_by_delivery AS (
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  bb.striker,
  b.non_striker,
  bs.runs_scored
FROM ball_by_ball b
LEFT JOIN ball_striker_link bb
  ON b.match_id = bb.match_id
  AND b.over_id = bb.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = bb.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = bb.innings_no
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
  ON b.match_id = bs.match_id
  AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
),
partnership_runs_by_pair_innings AS (
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  CASE WHEN b.striker <= b.non_striker THEN b.striker ELSE b.non_striker END AS player_a_id,
  CASE WHEN b.striker <= b.non_striker THEN b.non_striker ELSE b.striker END AS player_b_id,
  SUM(CASE WHEN b.striker <= b.non_striker THEN b.runs_scored ELSE 0 END) AS player_a_runs,
  SUM(CASE WHEN b.striker <= b.non_striker THEN 0 ELSE b.runs_scored END) AS player_b_runs,
  SUM(b.runs_scored) AS partnership_runs
FROM
  ball_bat_pair_by_delivery b
GROUP BY
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  player_a_id,
  player_b_id
),
match_level_max_partnership AS (
SELECT
  p.match_id,
  MAX(p.partnership_runs) AS max_partnership_runs
FROM partnership_runs_by_pair_innings p
GROUP BY p.match_id
)
SELECT
  p.match_id,
  CASE
    WHEN p.player_a_runs > p.player_b_runs THEN p.player_a_id
    WHEN p.player_b_runs > p.player_a_runs THEN p.player_b_id
    WHEN p.player_a_id > p.player_b_id THEN p.player_a_id
    ELSE p.player_b_id
  END AS player_1_id,
  CASE
    WHEN p.player_a_runs > p.player_b_runs THEN p.player_a_runs
    WHEN p.player_b_runs > p.player_a_runs THEN p.player_b_runs
    WHEN p.player_a_id > p.player_b_id THEN p.player_a_runs
    ELSE p.player_b_runs
  END AS player_1_runs,
  CASE
    WHEN p.player_a_runs > p.player_b_runs THEN p.player_b_id
    WHEN p.player_b_runs > p.player_a_runs THEN p.player_a_id
    WHEN p.player_a_id > p.player_b_id THEN p.player_b_id
    ELSE p.player_a_id
  END AS player_2_id,
  CASE
    WHEN p.player_a_runs > p.player_b_runs THEN p.player_b_runs
    WHEN p.player_b_runs > p.player_a_runs THEN p.player_a_runs
    WHEN p.player_a_id > p.player_b_id THEN p.player_b_runs
    ELSE p.player_a_runs
  END AS player_2_runs,
  p.partnership_runs
FROM partnership_runs_by_pair_innings p
JOIN match_level_max_partnership m
  ON p.match_id = m.match_id
 AND p.partnership_runs = m.max_partnership_runs
ORDER BY p.match_id ASC, player_1_id ASC

rows.question: Calculate the total number of wickets taken by each bowler (excluding run-outs and other dismissals not attributed to the bowler), their economy rate (total runs conceded divided by total overs bowled, considering only runs scored off the bat and ignoring any extra runs like wides and no-balls), their strike rate (average number of balls bowled per wicket taken), and their best bowling performance in a single match (the match with the most wickets taken by the bowler, formatted as "wickets-runs" where runs are the runs conceded excluding extras).
rows.pred_sql:
WITH bowler_wicket_events AS (
SELECT
  w.match_id,
  w.innings_no,
  w.over_id,
  w.ball_id,
  w.player_out,
  w.kind_out
FROM wicket_taken AS w
JOIN ball_by_ball AS b
  ON b.match_id = w.match_id
  AND b.over_id = w.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = w.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = w.innings_no
WHERE lower(w.kind_out) != 'run out'
  AND lower(w.kind_out) NOT IN ('recharge','retired hurt','obstructing the field','handled the ball')
),
ball_delivery_with_extras_and_bowler AS (
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.bowler,
  b.team_bowling,
  b.striker,
  COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) AS runs_scored,
  er.extra_type,
  er.extra_runs
FROM ball_by_ball b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
  ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
LEFT JOIN extra_runs er
  ON er.match_id = b.match_id
  AND er.over_id = b.over_id
  AND er.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND er.innings_no = b.innings_no
),
per_bowler_per_match_raw_counts AS (
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.bowler AS bowler,
  COUNT(*) AS total_balls_incl_illegal,
  SUM(CASE
        WHEN e.extra_type IN ('wides','noballs') THEN 0
        ELSE 1
      END) AS legal_balls,
  SUM(COALESCE(bs.runs_scored,0)) AS runs_conceded_off_bat,
  SUM(CASE WHEN w.kind_out IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_attributed
FROM ball_delivery_with_extras_and_bowler b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
  ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
LEFT JOIN extra_runs e
  ON e.match_id = b.match_id
  AND e.over_id = b.over_id
  AND e.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND e.innings_no = b.innings_no
LEFT JOIN bowler_wicket_events w
  ON w.match_id = b.match_id
  AND w.over_id = b.over_id
  AND w.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND w.innings_no = b.innings_no
GROUP BY
  b.bowler,
  b.match_id
)
SELECT
  p.player_id AS player_id,
  p.player_name AS player_name,
  SUM(pm.wickets_attributed) AS total_wickets,
  SUM(pm.legal_balls) AS balls_bowled,
  SUM(pm.runs_conceded_off_bat) AS runs_conceded_off_bat,
  CASE 
    WHEN SUM(pm.legal_balls) > 0 THEN (SUM(pm.runs_conceded_off_bat) * 6.0) / SUM(pm.legal_balls)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS economy_rate,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(pm.wickets_attributed) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(pm.legal_balls) AS REAL) / SUM(pm.wickets_attributed)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS strike_rate,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(pm.wickets_attributed) = 0 THEN '0-0'
    ELSE (
      SELECT CAST(bm.wickets_attributed AS TEXT) || '-' || CAST(bm.runs_conceded_off_bat AS TEXT)
      FROM per_bowler_per_match_raw_counts bm
      WHERE bm.bowler = pm_any.bowler
      ORDER BY bm.wickets_attributed DESC, bm.runs_conceded_off_bat ASC, bm.match_id ASC
      LIMIT 1
    )
  END AS best_match_performance
FROM per_bowler_per_match_raw_counts pm
JOIN per_bowler_per_match_raw_counts pm_any ON pm_any.bowler = pm.bowler
LEFT JOIN player p ON p.player_id = pm.bowler
GROUP BY p.player_id, p.player_name, pm.bowler
HAVING SUM(pm.legal_balls) > 0
ORDER BY total_wickets DESC, economy_rate ASC, player_id ASC

rows.question: List the bowlers (including their ID, first name, and last name), match number, game number, handicap score, tournament date, and location for only those bowlers who have won games with a handicap score of 190 or less at all three venues: Thunderbird Lanes, Totem Lanes, and Bolero Lanes. Only include the specific game records where they won with a handicap score of 190 or less at these three locations.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH bowler_score_game_rows AS (
SELECT
  Bowler_Scores.MatchID AS MatchID,
  Bowler_Scores.GameNumber AS GameNumber,
  Bowler_Scores.BowlerID AS BowlerID,
  Bowler_Scores.RawScore AS RawScore,
  Bowler_Scores.HandiCapScore AS HandiCapScore,
  Bowler_Scores.WonGame AS WonGame
FROM Bowler_Scores
),
match_game_to_tourney AS (
SELECT
  mg.MatchID,
  mg.GameNumber,
  tm.TourneyID,
  t.TourneyDate,
  t.TourneyLocation
FROM Match_Games AS mg
JOIN Tourney_Matches AS tm ON tm.MatchID = mg.MatchID
JOIN Tournaments AS t ON t.TourneyID = tm.TourneyID
),
bowler_win_handicap_by_location AS (
SELECT
  bsg.MatchID,
  bsg.GameNumber,
  bsg.BowlerID,
  mgt.TourneyID,
  mgt.TourneyLocation,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN bsg.WonGame = 1 AND bsg.HandiCapScore <= 190 THEN 1 END) AS qualifying_game_count
FROM
  bowler_score_game_rows AS bsg
JOIN
  match_game_to_tourney AS mgt
  ON bsg.MatchID = mgt.MatchID AND bsg.GameNumber = mgt.GameNumber
GROUP BY
  bsg.BowlerID,
  mgt.TourneyLocation,
  bsg.MatchID,
  bsg.GameNumber,
  mgt.TourneyID
)
SELECT
  bsr.BowlerID,
  b.BowlerFirstName,
  b.BowlerLastName,
  bsr.MatchID,
  bsr.GameNumber,
  bsr.HandiCapScore,
  mgt.TourneyDate,
  mgt.TourneyLocation
FROM bowler_score_game_rows AS bsr
JOIN match_game_to_tourney AS mgt
  ON bsr.MatchID = mgt.MatchID
  AND bsr.GameNumber = mgt.GameNumber
JOIN Bowlers AS b
  ON bsr.BowlerID = b.BowlerID
-- ensure only game rows that are wins with handicap <= 190 at the three locations
WHERE bsr.WonGame = 1
  AND bsr.HandiCapScore <= 190
  AND mgt.TourneyLocation IN ('Thunderbird Lanes', 'Totem Lanes', 'Bolero Lanes')
  -- ensure the bowler has at least one qualifying game at each of the three locations
  AND bsr.BowlerID IN (
    SELECT BowlerID
    FROM bowler_win_handicap_by_location
    WHERE TourneyLocation IN ('Thunderbird Lanes', 'Totem Lanes', 'Bolero Lanes')
    GROUP BY BowlerID
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT TourneyLocation) = 3
  )
ORDER BY
  bsr.BowlerID ASC,
  mgt.TourneyDate ASC,
  bsr.MatchID ASC,
  bsr.GameNumber ASC
